names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 26 Δεκεμβρίου, «Όσιος Κωνσταντίνος «ὁ ἐξ Ἰουδαίων»», with the rank word left off; the epithet «ὁ ἐξ Ἰουδαίων» is the page's own. The page says the name was given him at his baptism — «του έδωσαν το άγιο βάπτισμα και τον ονόμασαν Κωνσταντίνο» — and does not say what he was called before it.

attestations.note: The life page `/2796/` heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 26 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. **The page gives no year of any kind**, no emperor and no reign, so there is no `dates` object and none is inferred. It names Synada of Phrygia as his origin, the monastery of Phouvoution where he was baptised and tonsured, and Olympus, Myra of Lycia, Cyprus, Attaleia and Atroa among the places he preached in, Atroa being where he died in peace; no coordinate is proposed for any of them. He is none of the corpus's twenty-odd Constantines, who are kept on other days; the nearest in shape is `constantine-the-hagarene`, another convert named for his origin, and a different man on a different day. No hymn is printed. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.
